skill.name: configuring-better-auth
skill.description: Guide Better Auth OAuth 2.1 and OIDC server setup, Next.js SSO clients, PKCE flows, token handling, and JWKS verification.
skill.summary: Configure centralized Better Auth SSO servers and Next.js clients with OAuth 2.1, OIDC, PKCE, and JWKS.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Static results were dominated by false positives from Markdown, template literals, normal environment configuration, and expected OAuth network operations. Three findings remain confirmed: two remote MCP trust-boundary references and disabled signing-key encryption. Semantic review found serious flaws in token storage, state validation, JWT validation, redirects, cookies, and route protection.

remediation.issue: OAuth state is generated but never validated.
remediation.suggestion: Store state in a signed HttpOnly cookie and compare it with constant-time logic before token exchange. Reject missing or mismatched values.

remediation.issue: JWT checks omit issuer and audience.
remediation.suggestion: Pass the exact issuer and client identifier as jwtVerify options in every session, proxy, and API authorization path.

remediation.issue: The auth-server guide recommends localStorage for bearer tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Remove that pattern and use Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies managed by server routes. Keep access and refresh tokens unavailable to browser scripts.

remediation.issue: The proxy allows any pathname containing a period.
remediation.suggestion: Limit static bypasses to explicit framework asset prefixes and approved file extensions. Apply authentication to every other route.
Keep private-key encryption enabled and store its encryption secret outside the database. Document rotation and recovery procedures.

remediation.issue: Redirect targets are accepted from cookies and query parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only normalized relative paths or same-origin allowlisted URLs. Reject protocol-relative and absolute external targets.

remediation.issue: PKCE and token cookie examples omit important protections.
remediation.suggestion: Create short-lived PKCE state server-side and set every sensitive cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, path, and lifetime attributes.

remediation.issue: The setup connects agents to a third-party remote MCP service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the provider, data handling, and trust boundary before setup. Require explicit approval and offer a reviewed local alternative.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth State Is Not Validated
semantic_findings.description: The client stores state, but the callback never compares the returned value with the stored value. This enables login CSRF.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: State generation and callback parsing are present, but no equality check appears before token exchange.

semantic_findings.title: JWT Issuer And Audience Checks Are Missing
semantic_findings.description: JWT verification pins RS256 but omits issuer and audience checks in session and proxy paths. Tokens for another client could be accepted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both jwtVerify calls provide only an algorithm allowlist, while the main skill demonstrates the missing audience option.

semantic_findings.title: Bearer Tokens Are Stored In Local Storage
semantic_findings.description: The auth-server guide stores access and refresh tokens in localStorage and explicitly recommends that pattern. Same-origin scripts can read those bearer credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide directly reads and removes bearer tokens from localStorage, then states clients should only use that storage.

semantic_findings.title: Static Asset Rule Can Bypass Authentication
semantic_findings.description: The proxy treats every pathname containing a period as a static asset. Protected routes with periods can bypass authentication.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The unconditional pathname.includes check returns before token validation and is not limited to known asset directories or extensions.

semantic_findings.title: Post-Authentication Redirects Are Not Restricted
semantic_findings.description: Callback and refresh redirects accept cookie or query values without enforcing a local path. Absolute URLs can redirect users to attacker-controlled sites.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL constructor accepts absolute URLs, and neither redirect source is checked against an allowlist or same-origin policy.

semantic_findings.title: PKCE Verifier Cookies Are Script Readable
semantic_findings.description: The examples write PKCE verifiers through document.cookie without Secure or HttpOnly protection. Same-origin scripts can steal an active verifier.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples create the verifier cookie in browser JavaScript, making HttpOnly impossible and leaving Secure unset.

semantic_findings.title: Quick-Start Token Cookies Lack Security Attributes
semantic_findings.description: The main quick-start sets token cookies with only httpOnly. Missing Secure, SameSite, path, and lifetime controls weakens production token protection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cookie setters visibly omit attributes that the longer client guide later includes.

high_findings.title: Crypto seed/private key mention
high_findings.description: disablePrivateKeyEncryption: true, // Disable encryption for simplicity
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly disables private-key encryption for signing keys. A database or storage compromise could therefore expose usable OIDC signing material.

high_findings.title: OAuth State Is Not Validated
high_findings.description: The client stores state, but the callback never compares the returned value with the stored value. This enables login CSRF.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: State generation and callback parsing are present, but no equality check appears before token exchange.

high_findings.title: JWT Issuer And Audience Checks Are Missing
high_findings.description: JWT verification pins RS256 but omits issuer and audience checks in session and proxy paths. Tokens for another client could be accepted.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both jwtVerify calls provide only an algorithm allowlist, while the main skill demonstrates the missing audience option.

high_findings.title: Bearer Tokens Are Stored In Local Storage
high_findings.description: The auth-server guide stores access and refresh tokens in localStorage and explicitly recommends that pattern. Same-origin scripts can read those bearer credentials.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide directly reads and removes bearer tokens from localStorage, then states clients should only use that storage.

high_findings.title: Static Asset Rule Can Bypass Authentication
high_findings.description: The proxy treats every pathname containing a period as a static asset. Protected routes with periods can bypass authentication.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The unconditional pathname.includes check returns before token validation and is not limited to known asset directories or extensions.

content.user_title: Configure Better Auth OAuth and OIDC
content.value_statement: Centralized authentication requires coordinated server, client, token, and redirect settings. This skill provides Better Auth patterns for OAuth 2.1, OIDC, PKCE, and JWKS.
actual_capabilities: Guides Better Auth configuration as a centralized OIDC provider.
Shows public OAuth client registration with PKCE.
Provides Next.js callback, session, refresh, and logout patterns.
Explains JWT verification with remote JWKS keys.
Covers optional email verification and admin client registration.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to installed Better Auth and Next.js versions.
The skill does not deploy infrastructure or create provider accounts.
Production security still requires threat modeling, testing, and dependency review.
Several included security patterns need remediation before production use.

output_examples.output: A phased checklist covering database setup, exact client registration, PKCE, trusted origins, consent policy, key handling, and production verification.

output_examples.input: Add SSO login and refresh handling to an existing Next.js application.
output_examples.output: A file-level implementation plan for authorization, callback validation, protected sessions, token rotation, logout, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Review an existing Better Auth configuration before release.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review of redirect controls, state handling, token storage, JWT claims, cookie attributes, route coverage, and operational key practices.

best_practices: Use exact redirect URI allowlists and verify OAuth state before exchanging authorization codes.
Keep tokens in Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies and rotate refresh tokens server-side.
Verify JWT signature, issuer, audience, algorithm, expiration, and required claims on every authorization path.
anti_patterns: Do not store access or refresh tokens in localStorage.
Do not accept callback or return URLs without same-origin validation.
Do not disable signing-key encryption for convenience.

faq.question: Does this skill install Better Auth?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and example patterns. You must install compatible packages and apply changes within your project.

faq.question: When should I use a public OAuth client?
faq.answer: Use a public client when the application cannot protect a client secret, including browser and mobile applications. Require PKCE.

faq.question: Does the skill support confidential clients?
faq.answer: It discusses generated client secrets, but most client examples focus on public PKCE clients. Add server-side secret storage for confidential clients.

faq.question: Can it configure several SSO applications?
faq.answer: Yes. The provider guidance covers centralized authentication and separate exact redirect registrations for multiple applications.

faq.question: Does it verify JWTs securely by default?
faq.answer: Not fully. Some examples omit issuer and audience validation. Add those checks before using the patterns in production.

faq.question: Is the remote MCP service required?
faq.answer: No. The written guidance can be used without connecting to the third-party MCP endpoint.
